body:
We used an offline VM running a copy of our Agie Classic Cut 2S machine control. The control imported and plotted the native vertical punch used for comparison. CAMCraft CLI tests checked the tapered guide-height refusal and verified that it created no NC file. The VM test covered the vertical reference geometry only.

All controller runs were offline. No physical cut was made.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 09cf4df3a55f920434a4d4195c44d3adc669919a -->
Safety-tier review (read-only, not built). Head `09cf4df3a`. The trial merge with `origin/main` is clean (`git merge-tree`).

**Verdict: one blocker (an owed pin). The fix itself is correct.**

What is correct:
- `check_guide_span` (`crates/app/src/operation/wire_verify.rs:44-67`) runs in `wire_verdict`, before the slices. `wire_clause` reads it at `posting.rs:939`, before the post writes NC. Thus the GUI, the CLI and MCP all go through it.
- The span is the full work: the op planes, the part and the stock (`lo`/`hi` at lines 93-101). The issue case (a 12 mm work, upper guide Z5) now refuses by name.
- The frame is correct. The guides are read from `machine::of_setup`. The check adds `wcs_context` origin Z to each guide. This is the same frame as `guide_planes(machine, origin[2])` at `posting_wire.rs:159`. The message gives the work-frame heights.
- The check also applies to a vertical cut and a 4-axis cut, because the wire passes through the full work in all cases. A machine without stated guides is not refused. A taper on such a U/V machine is still refused at the command door.
- `work_above_the_upper_guide_blocks_the_post` and `guide_limits_use_the_setup_origin_and_include_stock_above_the_part` assert the text by name. The `post` helper asserts that no NC file is written on a refusal. The boundary (12.0 passes, 12.001 fails, at a 9.7 origin) is pinned.
- No golden changes. No `unwrap` or `panic` outside tests. The provenance line is present. `wire_verify.rs` is 158 lines. The decision file is present. Clean-room: no concern. The body is honest about the gate and the pre-existing `pocket3d_hsm` failure (#2371).

Blocker:
1. The lower-guide branch (`wire_verify.rs:53-58`, "work bottom Z... is below the lower guide Z...") has no pin that asserts its own text. The existing case `uv1` in `a_uv_offset_past_the_stroke_or_the_guides_is_refused_by_name` (`wire_taper.rs:169`, `lower_guide_z: 1.0`) now probably hits this new refusal first. It asserts only `outside the guides' reach`, which both refusals contain. Add a test (or extend `uv1`) that asserts `Punch1: work bottom Z0.000 is below the lower guide Z1.000` and that no NC is written.

Notes (not blockers):
- The old `judge_pose` refusal ("rides Z..., outside the guides' reach", `machine/wire_edm.rs:164-171`) is now defence in depth. When the guides are stated, the new check refuses first. Its pin in `uv1` now covers the new refusal instead. Say this in the test comment, so the next reader knows which refusal `uv1` pins.
- The non-finite guide refusal (`wire_verify.rs:50`) has no pin. A non-finite guide is improbable after `parse_mch`, so a pin is optional.

Tests a gate must run (crate `camcraft-app`):
- `--binary wire_taper`: all tests, in particular `work_above_the_upper_guide_blocks_the_post`, `guide_limits_use_the_setup_origin_and_include_stock_above_the_part`, `a_uv_offset_past_the_stroke_or_the_guides_is_refused_by_name`, `a_zero_taper_is_the_vertical_golden_byte_for_byte`, `a_tapered_punch_posts_its_golden_and_its_cl_shows_the_poses`.
- The other wire binaries that post on stated guides: `sodick_alc400g`, `edm_machine`, `solid_law_goldens` (the `wire_*` verdicts), and the other `wire_*` test binaries.
- clippy on `camcraft-app`.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 06925e8c4f4658975fc67199371c9824f0cac388 -->
**Re-check at 06925e8c4: read-only, not built (a maintainer-ordered review of a draft PR). floor: second review needed (this fixes a P1 wire refusal; a second safety-tier read is owed before merge).**

The head moved since the review at 09cf4df3a only by the merge of main 543204319 ("Local integration check"). Its remerge-diff is empty: no hand resolution, nothing dropped from either side. The review there stands unchanged, including the one blocker:

1. The lower-guide branch (`wire_verify.rs:56-59`, "work bottom Z... is below the lower guide Z...") still has no pin asserting its own text. Case `uv1` in `wire_taper.rs:170` asserts only `outside the guides' reach`, which both refusals contain. Add the named assertion and the no-NC check, or extend `uv1`.

Notes from the earlier review (not blockers) also stand. The merge author identity `CAMCraft gate <gate@localhost>` is a local automation identity - please push with your own git identity.

The coordinator session of NeoTech pushes a review fix to this draft PR (maintainer order: get the P1 PRs through).

- Push: `badb1966b` on top of your head `09cf4df3a`.
  - `32bfd1bdd`: merge of `origin/main` (no conflict).
  - `badb1966b`: `test(wire): pin the lower guide refusal by its own words`. The new test `work_below_the_lower_guide_blocks_the_post` (in `crates/app/tests/wire_taper.rs`) moves the lower guide to Z1 with a vertical punch. It asserts `Punch1: work bottom Z0.000 is below the lower guide Z1.000, outside the guides' reach`, and that no NC file is written. The refusal code is not changed.
- Gate (local, Windows, on this head): camcraft-app `wire_taper` (10 passed), `sodick_alc400g`, `edm_machine`, `solid_law_goldens` and the other 12 `wire_*` binaries all pass; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- Next: a short review of this test, then the maintainer decides the merge.

Correction to the comment above: the push of badb1966b was rejected, because a new head 06925e8c4 arrived first. Nothing of the coordinator is on the branch now. The coordinator merges the new head into its test commit, checks it again, and pushes only after that.

The coordinator pushed 9c4cfd2f4: a merge of your new head 06925e8c4 (a merge of main that main already holds; its remerge-diff is empty) into the test commit badb1966b. The tree of 9c4cfd2f4 is the same as badb1966b, so the gate result above applies: wire_taper 10 passed (with work_below_the_lower_guide_blocks_the_post), the 15 other wire/EDM binaries pass, clippy is clean. Next: a short review of the new test, then the maintainer decides the merge.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 9c4cfd2f4b36b64d2477b6bd59fa990f3c8f9453 -->
Review: clean, the blocker of 7052654467 is met.

Safety-tier delta review of the commits after 09cf4df3a (read-only, Opus).

- `badb1966b` adds `work_below_the_lower_guide_blocks_the_post` in `crates/app/tests/wire_taper.rs`.
  - The punch is vertical (taper 0.0). Thus no U/V refusal can occur first.
  - The fixture moves `lower_guide_z` from -5.0 to 1.0. The work bottom is Z0, so the work goes below the lower guide.
  - The test asserts the exact text `Punch1: work bottom Z0.000 is below the lower guide Z1.000, outside the guides' reach`. This is the text that `check_guide_span` (`wire_verify.rs`) makes.
  - The `post` helper asserts that no NC file is written when the post is refused.
- The refusal code does not change. `git diff 09cf4df3a 9c4cfd2f4 -- crates/app/src/operation/wire_verify.rs` is empty. The PR diff against main is the same as before, plus the 12 lines of the new test.
- No other check is weaker. The new commit adds lines only.
- The three merges (`06925e8c4`, `32bfd1bdd`, `9c4cfd2f4`) have an empty `git show --remerge-diff`. They change nothing by hand. The tree of `9c4cfd2f4` is the same as the tree of `badb1966b`.

Gate on `badb1966b` (local, Windows): camcraft-app `wire_taper` 10 passed. 15 other wire/EDM test binaries pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app` is clean.

Ready and merge: the coordinator flags head 9c4cfd2f4 ready and merges it with the maintainer's word. Reviews: the Opus safety-tier review (comment 7052654467) and its re-review on this head (comment 7053212157, clean: the owed lower-guide pin is met). Gate (local, Windows, on the same tree badb1966b): camcraft-app wire_taper 10 passed, the 15 other wire/EDM binaries pass, clippy -p camcraft-app clean. Heavy lanes: not run, covered by the cut gate.
